b: Real estate prospecting software helps agents capture and follow up with inbound, referral, and website leads. It gives every contact an owner, every conversation a history, and every opportunity a next step.

Managing multiple lead sources sounds simple — until a Zillow inquiry lands in one inbox and a referral arrives by text while an agent is at a showing. A good system pulls those threads together. The result is faster follow-up and a pipeline that everyone, from solo agent to brokerage owner, can actually see.

This guide explains which features matter most, how to choose between a niche real estate CRM and flexible sales software, and how eight platforms compare across key capabilities. It also covers how to prioritize leads using first-party activity, connect property-search behavior to contact records, and manage calling, texting, and email follow-up responsibly.

What Real Estate Prospecting Software Should Help You Do

Real estate teams use prospecting software to improve response time and pipeline visibility. At minimum, real estate prospecting software should capture leads, assign follow-up, preserve communication history, and show where each opportunity stands. Be aware: prospecting software can’t fix a vague follow-up process. Prospecting software will make a good process easier to repeat and harder to hide missed handoffs.
The practical must-haves for real estate prospecting software are:
Lead capture. Zillow and Realtor.com inquiries, IDX registrations, open-house sign-ins, home valuation requests, sign calls, and referrals should flow into one database without manual re-entry.
Lead routing. Teams should be able to assign leads by ZIP code, price range, buyer or seller status, language, round-robin rules, or the agent currently on call.
Property context. The contact record should show which listing generated the inquiry, which homes the lead viewed or saved, and whether the lead engaged with a property alert.

Repeatable follow-up. Templates, task queues, reminders, and approved automations should support new inquiries, no-response leads, open-house attendees, long-term buyers, past clients, and referral opportunities.
A real estate pipeline. Useful stages might include new lead, attempted contact, nurture, appointment set, active buyer or seller, under contract, and closed.
Team accountability. Team leads need visibility into speed-to-lead, contact rates, appointments, lead reassignment, closed transactions, and lead-source performance.
Consent and preference records. The system should retain opt-in details where required and apply opt-outs across the relevant channels.
How to Choose Real Estate Prospecting Software

There’s no one right choice when it comes to prospecting software. The most important thing to consider is how it fits into your lead sources and daily follow-up habits. Before comparing demos, answer six questions:
Where do leads come from? List every portal, IDX site, form, ad platform, open-house app, and referral channel that needs to connect.

How should leads be assigned? A team may route new inquiries to an inside sales agent (ISA), buyer’s agent, listing agent, agent on call, or shared lead pond. Check whether untouched leads can be reassigned automatically.
What context follows the contact? Confirm that the original property inquiry, saved listings, calls, texts, emails, notes, financing status, and next appointment remain attached to the record.

How much real estate functionality should be native? IDX search, property alerts, transaction management, and listing marketing are convenient in an industry-specific platform. A flexible CRM may require integrations, but can support more customized sales processes and other departments.
What is the full cost? Include onboarding, extra users, calling and texting, IDX, advertising, data migration, and required add-ons, not just the number on the pricing page.
For broader context, these guides to sales automation and real estate lead generation can help teams map the process before buying the platform.
The eight products below range from flexible sales software to real estate operating systems. The fit ratings are editorial assessments based on each vendor’s published features and target customer.
1. HubSpot Smart CRM and Sales Hub

Sales Hub lets real estate professionals build custom pipelines for buyers, sellers, and referral partners, with tools like email templates and sales sequences to keep leads moving from first inquiry to closing. Smart CRM is the system of record underneath it, keeping contact details, client conversations, tasks, and deal history in one place.

Sales Hub adds email templates and tracking, calling, pipelines, and, on Professional and Enterprise plans, sales sequences. The lead management and prospecting workspace is available on Professional and Enterprise plans.
Pricing: HubSpot offers a free CRM edition; paid Sales Hub and Smart CRM plans vary by product, billing term, seats, bundles, onboarding, and promotions

What I like: HubSpot gives a growing team room to define its own process. A brokerage can keep a straightforward buyer-and-seller pipeline today, then add recruiting, referral partner, lender, or post-close workflows without moving those relationships into another system.
Keep in mind: HubSpot doesn’t provide a native IDX website or property-alert engine. Teams that need those features should confirm the integration and data flow before committing.

Follow Up Boss is a real estate CRM and lead management platform that pulls leads from websites, portals, and ad platforms into one place so agents can follow up quickly. It’s best for real estate teams that receive leads from many sources and need to route them fast. Its Grow plan connects lead sources, distributes contacts to the right agents, organizes follow-up with Smart Lists (dynamic lists of contacts who need attention), and runs Action Plans (automated sequences of tasks, emails, and texts). Agents can also send texts and emails from inside the platform, and reporting tracks agent and source performance.

Pricing: Grow costs $58 per user per month when billed annually. Calling costs extra on Grow. Pro costs $416 per month for 10 users and includes unlimited calling and texting; Platform costs $833 per month for 30 users.

What I like: The platform stays close to the moment a lead comes in. Lead-source connections, assignment rules, follow-up plans, and team reporting all support the same goal: getting the right agent into the conversation quickly.
Keep in mind: Teams should price the plan they will actually use. A low per-user entry point can look different once calling, texting, or a larger group is included.

BoldTrail is a real estate platform from Inside Real Estate (formerly kvCORE) that combines IDX websites, lead generation, a Smart CRM, and marketing automation, with separate BackOffice and Recruit modules for brokerage operations. Its Front Office platform combines configurable IDX websites, a lead engine, behavioral insights, CRM tools, and automated follow-up.
Pricing: BoldTrail doesn’t publish standard subscription prices. The company directs buyers to request a package and quote based on their market, team, and selected products.

What I like: The appeal lies in BoldTrail’s breadth. A brokerage trying to reduce the number of vendors behind its website, CRM, lead nurturing, recruiting, and operations can evaluate these pieces together rather than building each connection separately.
Keep in mind: Breadth also makes implementation more consequential. Buyers should ask which modules are included, how data migration works, and what ongoing administration the system requires.

Rechat is an AI-powered real estate platform that brings CRM, marketing design, and transaction management into one system for brokerages and their agents. Rechat is best for brokerages that want contact management, listing marketing, and transaction workflows in a connected platform. Its People product manages contacts, lead assignment, tasks, calendars, and automated Flows; Studio creates branded digital and print marketing; Deals tracks listings, offers, checklists, and closings.
Rechat sells directly to brokerages and uses custom pricing. A brokerage can adopt individual products or the wider platform.

What I like: Rechat connects work that agents normally scatter across several apps. A lead can live in the CRM while the team builds listing materials and tracks the transaction in the same product family. That is especially useful when brand consistency matters across many agents.
Keep in mind: Solo agents generally access Rechat through a brokerage relationship, so independent agents should confirm availability before putting it on a shortlist.

Wise Agent is a web-based CRM built for real estate agents that manages contacts, automates follow-up, and organizes transactions on a flat-rate plan. Wise Agent is best for solo agents and small teams that want a real estate-specific CRM at a relatively accessible price. It includes lead pipelines, contact summaries, drip campaigns, email and text logging, transaction checklists, commission reporting, and more than 100 integrations.
Wise Agent’s “five team members” pricing does not include five independent user accounts. Teams that need individual permissions and activity attribution should include extra logins in the budget.
Pricing: The CRM costs $42 per month billed annually. That price includes up to five team members on a shared login; separate logins and some messaging features are paid add-ons.

What I like: Wise Agent covers a surprising amount of day-to-day real estate work without forcing a solo agent into a large platform purchase. The flat base price is also easier to understand than a stack of per-seat charges.

Lofty (formerly Chime) is an AI-powered real estate platform that combines a CRM, IDX websites, lead generation, and marketing automation for agents, teams, and brokerages. Lofty is best for agents, teams, and brokerages that want lead generation, an IDX website, CRM, property alerts, and multi-step follow-up in one real estate platform. Its Smart Plans can coordinate email, text, calls, and direct mail, while the CRM uses lead activity to surface opportunities.
Pricing: Lofty uses quote-based pricing for its core platform and does not offer a free trial. Advertising and some services carry additional fees, so buyers should request a full package breakdown.

What I like: The IDX experience and CRM share context. When listing searches, property interests, alerts, and follow-up sit together, an agent has more useful first-party signals than a generic “new lead” notification.

Keep in mind: An all-in-one system is a bigger commitment than a standalone CRM. Teams should test website flexibility, data export, advertising fees, and migration support as carefully as the contact-management features.

BoomTown is a lead generation and CRM platform for real estate teams and brokerages that combines IDX websites, a predictive CRM, and human lead concierge services. BoomTown is best for established teams and brokerages that want to combine lead generation, IDX websites, lead management, and a predictive real estate CRM. The CRM tracks consumer activity, surfaces likely opportunities, and provides deal and pipeline views. BoomTown also offers Success Assurance, which pairs software with lead-concierge support.
Pricing: BoomTown packages its software in Launch, Core, Grow, and Advance tiers, but does not publish standard prices. Buyers need a custom quote.

What I like: BoomTown treats follow-up as an operating system rather than an isolated contact database. The mix of website behavior, opportunity signals, agent activity, and optional concierge support can suit a team with meaningful lead volume.
BoomTown is likely more platform than a solo agent needs. Ask what is included in the quoted package, which services are optional, and how advertising spend affects total cost.

Note: BoomTown is owned by Inside Real Estate, which acquired it in 2023 and has said it is being folded into BoldTrail, so availability and features may change; confirm current plans with the vendor before buying.

Vulcan7 is a real estate prospecting platform that delivers daily seller leads, such as expired listings and for-sale-by-owner (FSBO) properties, alongside a built-in power dialer and CRM. Vulcan7 is best for agents whose prospecting process is built around scheduled calling. Every plan includes a power dialer, real estate CRM, call logging, follow-up tools, and seller-lead products; higher tiers add more dialer seats, numbers, lead types, and AI call summaries.
Pricing: Vulcan7 now uses custom pricing based on the plan, market, lead types, and billing term.

What I like: The dialer and CRM share the same workflow. Calls, dispositions, notes, emails, and next steps can remain attached to the contact rather than being copied across systems. Teams comparing this category may also find HubSpot’s sales dialer guide useful.

Vulcan7 is best suited for outbound seller prospecting rather than inbound, referral, and website-lead management. Agents using its calling and texting tools need a well-defined compliance process, including consent where required, suppression checks, and prompt handling of opt-outs.

For teams that want flexible lead follow-up without committing to a real estate-specific operating system, Sales Hub brings contact history, tasks, sequences, calling, and deal tracking into one connected platform.
Niche Real Estate CRM vs. Flexible Sales Software

A niche real estate CRM usually provides industry features faster. Flexible sales software gives a team more control over its pipeline, automation, reporting, and connections to other departments. The better choice depends on how much of the real estate stack needs to be managed by one vendor.

HubSpot suits teams that want separate buyer, seller, recruiting, referral, and partnership pipelines within a single configurable system. Real estate platforms such as Lofty, BoldTrail, Rechat, or BoomTown work better when IDX behavior, property alerts, listing marketing, and transaction management need to work immediately with minimal configuration.
